blocks.text: Design the browser side of a global live-comment stream that preserves resumable sequence order, moderation revisions, and the reader's follow-mode anchor during bursts.

blocks.title: Use RADIO
blocks.text: Requirements define the audience, peak event shape, ordering and resume guarantees, follow-mode behavior, moderation authority, accessibility, and measurable success criteria.

What you are solving:
A real-time comment stream beside a live video. It must stay readable, ordered, and responsive during spikes (e.g., big moments), while supporting moderation and user interaction.

Decision surface:
- Real-time delivery (WebSocket/SSE)
- Buffering + batching to avoid re-render storms
- Virtualized list rendering
- Ordering + dedupe strategy
- Auto-scroll vs user scroll behavior
- Moderation UX and error handling

steps.title: 1) Open stream
steps.text: Load the latest N comments and establish a live connection.

steps.title: 2) Ingest events
steps.text: Validate and reduce every authoritative event; coalesce store commits only enough to keep the interface responsive.

steps.title: 3) Render safely
steps.text: Render a virtualized list and keep DOM size bounded.

steps.title: 4) User scrolls
steps.text: Pause auto-scroll when the user scrolls up; show a “new comments” badge.

steps.title: 5) Moderation
steps.text: Apply hide, mute, and removal updates without breaking sequence order, the reader's anchor, or the pending-new-comment count.

blocks.title: Clarifying questions
items: How many comments per second at peak?
Strict ordering vs eventual ordering?
Auto-scroll always on, or pause on user scroll?
Do we show sender badges, avatars, emojis, GIFs?
What moderation actions are required?
What freshness budget should be tested for each device and network cohort?
Any slow-mode or rate-limit rules?

blocks.title: Non-functional expectations
items: Smooth scrolling under bursts, verified with field frame and long-task data.
DOM size bounded via virtualization.
Graceful fallback on slow networks.
Consistent UX across devices.
Observable latency + error metrics.

blocks.title: Follow-mode UI states
rows: User scrolled up; show “new comments” badge

items.label: End-to-end latency
items.helperText: Begin with a testable freshness hypothesis and revise from field data.

items.label: Batch window
items.helperText: Tune burst coalescing from freshness and render evidence.

items.label: DOM cap
items.helperText: Choose retained and rendered bounds from memory and navigation tests.

blocks.title: Critical trade-off
blocks.text: Lower latency means more frequent renders. You must justify batching and explain how you avoid re-render storms during spikes.

blocks.title: Explicit assumptions
items: Peak comment rate, burst duration, and how long sequence gaps remain repairable.
Moderation states, revision ordering, and whether removed bodies become tombstones.
Follow-mode policy when the reader scrolls away from the live edge.
Composer slow mode, optimistic echo, and reconnect behavior on constrained devices.

blocks.title: Follow, moderation, and recovery constraints
items: Auto-scroll behavior when the user scrolls up.
Visible new-items indicator or badge.
Moderation actions that can remove items without breaking layout.
Clear empty/error states.

blocks.text: The browser owns stream resume, comment merge, moderation overlays, follow mode, viewport anchoring, bounded rendering, and composer feedback. Global distribution, authoritative moderation decisions, and durable comment storage stay behind abstract resumable event and command contracts.
